newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal starts talks with France Telecom.
newsitem.headline: Senegal starts talks with France Telecom.

text.p: Senegal has started formal talks with France Telecom on the sale of a one-third stake in telecommunications company SONATEL, Senegal's economy minister said.
"Now we have started talks with France Telecom over the privatisation of SONATEL," Papa Ousmane Sacko told state television on Wednesday night.
On April 16 Senegal canceled a provisional deal with a consortium led by Sweden's Telia Overseas on the purchase of a strategic stake in SONATEL worth 70 billion CFA francs ($122 million).
France Telecom had made an offer of 65 billion CFA. "We are at the very beginning of the talks," the minister added.
He said Senegal broke with the Swedish-led consortium because it wanted a get-out clause after seven years, despite a written agreement commiting it for 20 years.
The remaining shares will be sold to private Senegalese and other African investors with 10 percent allocated to SONATEL staff.
Senegal has announced a liberalisation of its cellular telephone sector next year, with January the target date for the start of a second network.
SONATEL started the West African nation's first cellular telephone service last October, using a GSM system.
SONATEL has a capital base of 50 billion CFA francs and an annual turnover of more than 60 billion.
